pergunta: Of which population is E_sigma[Err_sigma] (mean MAE over split draws of the retained test set, which is what the protocol reports) an estimator, and with what bias relative to the MAE of the whole domain? Does the mean weighted by p_i^te (Sum p_i e_i / Sum p_i) reproduce E_sigma[Err_sigma] closely enough to become the formal definition of the estimand in Sec.3? Does the Horvitz-Thompson correction (1 split draw, weighted by 1/p_i^te) reduce the bias enough to enter the article?
alegacao: A3 (estimand drift) + formal estimand of Sec.3 (D6-i)
hipotese: with FIXED e_i (predictors without training, constant and FSPL calibrated on the valid training nodes, calibrated ONCE on the reference split seed=42), Sum p_i e_i/Sum p_i (ratio of expectations, using p_i^te from test 1.6) approximates E_sigma[Err_sigma] (expectation of the ratio) better than the MAE of the whole domain; the single-draw Horvitz-Thompson correction may or may not reduce the bias relative to the whole-domain MAE
metodo_fixado: same 4 cells and 100 seeds as test 1.6 (identical split, reuse of the same partitions per split draw); e_i = |y_i - yhat_i| in RSSI for EVERY node of the domain (3600x3600), fixed by ONE calibration on the training set of split seed=42 (constant=median(RSSI_train); calibrated FSPL (b) = offset by the median of the VALID training nodes, frozen okumura/fspl formula from scripts_congelados/baselines_v2_por_particao.py); per population (valid: PL<299, sentinel: PL>=299, all): (a) whole-domain MAE = mean(e_i) over all nodes of the population; (b) mean over the 100 split draws of MAE(e_i) restricted to the retained test set V_te(sigma); (c) Sum_{i in population} p_i^te e_i / Sum_{i in population} p_i^te (p_i^te from test 1.6, same 100 draws); (d) per-draw Horvitz-Thompson: Sum_{i in V_te(sigma) intersect population} e_i/p_i^te / Sum_{i in V_te(sigma) intersect population} 1/p_i^te, mean and std over the 100 draws.
definicoes: vies_protocolo = (b) - (a); vies_HT = mean(d) - (a); (b)-(c) measures the ratio of expectations (c) vs the expectation of the ratio (b). Everything in dB (RSSI), 3 decimal places.
limiar_aceitacao: (c) reproduces (b) within <0.05 dB in >=3 of the 4 cells (then Sum p_i e_i/Sum p_i becomes the publishable formal definition of the estimand in Sec.3); the HT correction enters the article only if |vies_HT| < |vies_protocolo|/2 in >=3 of the 4 cells AND in the three populations (valid, sentinel, all) simultaneously
refutacao: if (c) diverges from (b) by >=0.05 dB in >=2 of the 4 cells, the ratio of expectations is not declared equivalent to the expectation of the ratio and Sec.3 must record the difference as a note, not as an identity; if the HT bias-reduction condition fails in any population or in <3 cells, the HT correction LEAVES the article (only the definition + the reported bias remain)
